vsam.why: base/cntl/adef121.jcl DEFINE2: DATA(... KEYS(21 0) RECORDSIZE(64 64)); the engine's facts do not read KEYS / RECORDSIZE inside the DATA component, so the case states them

scenarios.name: add-endowment
scenarios.why: request E: with-profits / equities / managed fund / fund name and CA-E-LIFE-ASSURED (31 bytes) cut to WF's 30

scenarios.name: add-house
scenarios.why: request H: property type, bedrooms, value, postcode, and the 20-byte house name cut to 9

scenarios.name: add-motor
scenarios.why: request M: make, model, value (999999, the PIC 9(6) maximum), registration

scenarios.name: add-commercial
scenarios.why: request C: postcode, status 9(4), and the 255-byte customer cut to 31

scenarios.name: add-other-type
scenarios.why: request-id(4:1) = '9': WHEN OTHER blanks WF-POLICY-DATA; the key starts with a digit

scenarios.name: add-key-zero
scenarios.why: boundary: customer 0 / policy 0, the lowest M key

scenarios.name: add-key-max
scenarios.why: boundary: customer and policy 9999999999; bedrooms 999, value 99999999 (the PIC maxima)

scenarios.name: add-same-numbers-other-type
scenarios.why: customer 3 / policy 5 exist as an E record; under H the key differs, so the WRITE is NORMAL and both records stay

notes: GenApp's VSAM 'add policy' (LGAPVS01, LINKed by LGAPDB01): the policy key is CA-REQUEST-ID(4:1) (the type: E/H/M/C) + CA-CUSTOMER-NUM + CA-POLICY-NUM; an EVALUATE on the type moves that type's fields into WF-POLICY-DATA (WHEN OTHER: spaces), then EXEC CICS WRITE FILE('KSDSPOLY') FROM(WF-Policy-Info) LENGTH(64) RIDFLD(WF-Policy-Key) KEYLENGTH(21); on NORMAL it GOBACKs. Each scenario's KSDSPOLY is compared after the task. Every non-NORMAL RESP in this program goes to WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE, whose first act is EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('LGSTSQ') (GenApp's TS/TD error logger, defined in the CSD); the equivalence harness runs one program and has no port of LGSTSQ, so a scenario that reaches it is refused (Unsupported: LINK PROGRAM(LGSTSQ)). The error paths -- DUPREC on an existing key, NOSPACE / NOTOPEN / IOERR, CA-RETURN-CODE '80' -- are therefore NOT exercised here; they need LGSTSQ modelled (or ported) first. Keys: WF-POLICY-KEY is the request-type byte followed by 20 digits, so every key mixes a letter and digits; the WHEN OTHER scenario puts a digit in that first byte (digits sort before letters in ASCII, after them in EBCDIC). No browse is issued, so no key order is exercised (the comparison sorts each side's records by key bytes). Data: ksdspoly.txt is built from GenApp's own sample policies (base/cntl/db2cre.jcl's policy rows joined with their endowment / house / motor / commercial rows), laid out as WF-POLICY-INFO (request-type letter + customer + policy number, then the type's 43 bytes) -- the record LGAPVS01 writes; policy 7 (type C, no commercial row) is left out.
